Hoge","extract":"Joseph Pendleton Hoge (December 15, 1810 – August 14, 1891) was an American politician, lawyer, and judge. He was a member of the United States House of Representatives from Illinois.


== Biography ==
Born in Steubenville, Ohio, Hoge attended the common schools and graduated from Jefferson College (now Washington & Jefferson College). He studied law and was admitted to the bar in 1836. He moved to Galena 1836 and practiced law. He held several local offices.
With the help of the Mormon citizens of Nauvoo, who voted for him en masse, Hoge was elected by Illinois's 6th congressional district as a Democrat to the Twenty-eighth and Twenty-ninth Congresses (from March 4, 1843 to March 3, 1847). He was not a candidate for renomination in 1846. He resumed the practice of law in Galena.
Hoge moved to California in 1853 and continued the practice of law. He was an unsuccessful candidate for election to the United States Senate in 1867. He served as president of the state constitutional convention in 1878 and the board of freeholders in 1880. He served as judge of the San Francisco County Superior Court from January 1, 1889, until his death in the city on August 14, 1891.
